subject: Urgent: p99 spikes on hosted API for long-context workloads (32k) - customer escalation
messages:
From: Diana Perez <diana@acmeai.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: platform-sre@acmeai.com
Date: Thu, 14 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Spike in p99/p99.9 on hosted API after 32k context rollout

Marcus —

We're seeing major regressions starting ~May 13 after we switched a subset of traffic to the 32k context path. High-level: p95 is OK-ish but p99/p99.9 jumps to 8-12s (was ~700ms), error rate for our streaming endpoints shows ~4.7% 503/timeout, and overall throughput has dropped ~30% on the busiest tier. This is directly impacting our chat UI and we have customers seeing sessions time out.

We run a mix of 8k/16k/32k prompts (most requests hit 16k, but our long-document index produces many 32k sequences during nightly processing). We can reproduce with a few synthetic requests hitting the 32k path. Logs attached (acme_logs_20260514.zip). Can you escalate to engineering? We need an interim mitigation and an ETA for a root cause.

-Diana
Director, Platform — Acme AI

Attachments: acme_logs_20260514.zip

From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: Diana Perez <diana@acmeai.com>
Cc: olga_petrov@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 14 May 2026 09:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike in p99/p99.9 on hosted API after 32k context rollout

Diana — thanks for the heads up and for the logs. I'm escalating immediately and scheduling a bridge. Initial ask for data from you: sample request IDs (if possible), approximate time windows where you see timeouts, and whether you saw any increased token churn or longer completions.

Olga / SRE team, please triage traces and perf dashboards first — prioritize 32k-context routing paths and KV-cache behavior. Rishi, bringing you in for visibility and exec escalation. Priyom, please loop in account team for any credit/terms asks.

Planned immediate actions:
- Open an incident and start live traces on affected hosts.
- Canary a routing change to limit 32k requests to dedicated capacity (if possible) to buy time.
- Collect perf snapshots and flamegraphs; attach to JIRA INF-4829.

I will update customer within 30 minutes with a temporary mitigation plan.

-Marcus
Sr. Director, Customer Ops — Redwood Inference

From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: Diana Perez <diana@acmeai.com>
Date: Thu, 14 May 2026 09:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in p99/p99.9 on hosted API after 32k context rollout

On Thu, May 14, 2026 at 09:25, marcus_lin@redwood.com wrote:
> Diana — thanks for the heads up and for the logs. I'm escalating immediately and scheduling a bridge. Initial ask for data from you: sample request IDs (if possible)...

We've pulled the traces and the perf dashboard (attached) shows a clear pattern: long-context requests (16k->32k path) produce much larger KV-cache working sets and trigger cache eviction + re-compilation behavior on some hosts. Two likely contributors:

1) Kernel selector misrouting for extremely long sequences — some models fall back to a slower execution path after certain sequence lengths, which inflates tail latency.
2) Continuous batching + cache eviction interaction — large requests monopolize GPU memory leading to more page thrashing and packetized errors under peak load.

Immediate mitigations I recommend we can apply via config without a full deploy:
- Temporarily cap max_context_sent_to_host to 16k for incoming 32k requests and force fallback to a 'split-chunk' service (reduces single-request memory pressure).
- Turn off large-request continuous batching for the affected pool (reduces head-of-line blocking).
- Route long-context traffic for Acme to a small dedicated pool (reserved capacity) for next 6 hours.

I'll attach a perf snapshot and a sample flamegraph. If we need a code fix it looks like INF-4829 (kernel selector and cache handling) will be the hotfix.

-Attachments: perf-dashboard-20260514.png

-Olga
SRE Lead — Redwood Inference

From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: Diana Perez <diana@acmeai.com>
Cc: olga_petrov@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 14 May 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in p99/p99.9 on hosted API after 32k context rollout

Diana — quick update and proposed temporary plan:

1) We can immediate-canary the routing change to send Acme's 32k requests to dedicated capacity for the next 6-12 hours. This will isolate them from shared pools and should remove the eviction interaction.
2) We'll apply a config cap so any single request sent to a shared host will be split at 16k (split-chunk fallback). This is reversible.
3) Olga's team will disable large-request continuous batching on the affected pool for the short window.

If you approve, we'll put this in place now and monitor p99/p99.9 and error rate. Expected customer-visible improvement within 10-20 minutes of routing change; if not, we'll open a shadow canary and escalate to a kernel-level rollback.

Also looping Priyom on commercial ask — please review compensation/credits if SLA breach is likely.

-Marcus
